Want to dip into a realistic military shooter, without learning a textbook of info and a piano length of controls? Try this out! It's Call of Duty without the jump corner shots and one knife kills, suppressing fire and smokes are scary effective and working together is (while not needed all the time) is essential. Full auto is mostly wasteful and reloading is staged from ejecting the mag to inserting a new one. Mod support is building in the game and it just recently dropped on to consoles. While it may have a rocky start, it's now playable and running smoothly after some optimization updates. If you can run Unreal 4 games, you shouldn't have much issue. Of course, I could be wrong...

Original Review Below:

2019:
My favourite game on Steam.
Co-op Vs Bots is my scene; and I loved the original Insurgency too.
Looks great, sounds great, feels great.

Give it a shot.

The guns are heavy.
The sounds are loud and scary.
The animations are smooth.
The voice acting is authentic.
The game modes are fun.
The devs are listening to feedback.

Although it was buggy at launch, I still would have said the same thing.
It's a quality experience.

The sense of community from Insurgency was lost, and the map quality was better in the original. No gear was a thing. It's still a good game, though (but to the devs: fk u for abandoning the first game without support after just 6 months). Maybe I'm just experiencing the duck syndrome.

very hard, but also very rewarding when you do get good enough to compete. I had fun with it. my favorite part of the game was the games verses bots, because in theory playing against them first helps new players get used to controls before playing against other players.

If youre thinking of getting this game i would recommend it not quite as hardcore as tarkov or squad but more hardcore than call of duty, dont need to spray someone with half a mag to have to kill them. Everything seems to be balanced pretty decently from what ive seen so far, not to mention peoples heads explode when you headshot them

This is the best shooter I've ever played. If you're sick of other players in other shooters surviving a .50 BMG shot to the chest, this game is for you! An enemy is behind a wall? NO PROBLEM! Spray the wall with your M240B and you may not only hear the crying screams for mercy of your enemies on the other side, but maybe your teammates as well, so be careful!

Excellent FPS with really satisfying gunplay which is a mix of run and gun and a slower more tactical style.
The sound design is really great with the snap of bullets whizzing passed your head and guns are LOUD. It reminds me of that scene in The Rock where Sean Connery is mag-dumping bad guys and Nic Cage is shouting but you can't hear a word he says over the gunfire.
The community is chill too, i've barely encountered any try-hards or cry babies like in some other FPS games.
There's also an achievement for killing someone with a door.

It's cool, i like it.

I love the direction that Sandstorm goes with immersion. I love immersion and i encourage the developers/staff for Sandstorm to continue to push those boundaries. Graphics and sounds feel great. As far as critiques are concerned, I think it would be a good idea to push the boundaries of the enemy AI system. I'm personally more of a PvE player rather than PvP. The enemy AI are good in terms of being able to shoot their gun...sometimes... I'm not complaining about that. What i do want to see is better tactics from the AI. (ex. better maneuver tactics, cover to cover, leaning. I believe this can help the developers vision with immersion because it will be more realistic. Maybe have a difficulty level set in place for players who want a tougher experience. (Or have dedicated servers with set difficulty levels and have it be an option in the the "match preferences") Also, most importantly, add more game types.... especially with Cooperative mode. Its fun, but it can get old. Mix it up, add more content and game modes. (ex. Survival mode/more maps) I definitely recommend this game, but it still needs more content.

It is just the right mix of casual mixed with intense realism. A go to if you want the simplicity of call of duty but the teamwork, pace, and grittiness of something like ARMA or SQUAD.

Server stability issues seems to have been resolved, updated lighting made night maps playable, and I'm impressed they're still pushing out content 8yrs after release AND after getting gutted by Embracer. Solid gunplay and movement, realistic enough weapons and character customization; what more could you ask for out of a Tactical FPS?
